reasons: Only 4 of 15 sections were supplied in the packet, so the other 11 tests could not be reviewed.
The rules behind the placements are in a module not shown here.

terms.meaning: where each piece of equipment is placed in the 3D site
a basic shape used to draw a part, such as a box, cylinder or turbine
distance measured along a linear project such as a road or pipeline
a raised structure that carries pipes across a process plant

sections.name: File setup
sections.title: Test setup
sections.what: Brings in the two layout functions used by the tests.
sections.why: Gives the tests access to the layout rules.

sections.name: _by_leaf
sections.title: Find placements by name
sections.what: Returns the placements whose path contains a given word.
sections.why: Lets tests pick out items such as all erection steps.
sections.watch_out: Matches any path containing the text, so a short word could match extra items.

sections.name: test_wind_turbines_stand_in_number_order_with_foundations_underneath
sections.title: Wind turbine order and foundations
sections.what: Builds ten turbines and a substation breaker, then checks each turbine keeps its number order, its foundation sits under it, and the breaker is beside the turbines.
sections.why: Confirms wind layouts read in a sensible order.
sections.watch_out: Depends on the number order rule in the layout module.

sections.name: test_solar_blocks_form_a_grid_with_matching_inverters_beside_them
sections.title: Solar blocks in a grid with inverters
sections.what: Builds nine solar blocks with piles, arrays and inverters, then checks the shapes are right, the blocks form a grid, and each inverter sits beside its block.
sections.why: Confirms solar layouts are grid-based with inverters next to their blocks.
sections.watch_out: Tolerance values such as the one used for alignment are fixed and may need changing if spacing changes.

sections.name: test_process_units_line_a_pipe_rack_spine
sections.title: Process units line up along a pipe rack
sections.what: Checks that refinery units and tanks are placed as separate items and that the two process units sit on opposite sides of the main pipe rack.
sections.why: Likely reason: the layout is meant to look like a real plant, where equipment hangs off a shared pipe rack. Reason not stated in the code.
sections.watch_out: If placement rules put both units on the same side of the rack, this check fails.

sections.name: test_mine_reads_in_flow_order_from_pit_to_tailings
sections.title: Mine items follow the flow from pit to tailings
sections.what: Confirms a gold mine's items are placed left to right in the order material moves: pit, crusher, conveyor, stockpile, mill, then tailings.
sections.why: Likely reason: so the site reads in the same order as the mining process.
sections.watch_out: Moving any one step out of order in the placement rules breaks the reading order.

sections.name: test_linear_projects_build_up_in_layers_along_chainage
sections.title: Highway sections build up in layers
sections.what: Checks that each highway section's earthworks sit lower than its asphalt paving, that sections are placed in numeric order along the road, and that a bridge is recognised as a bridge.
sections.why: Likely reason: so a road looks built from the ground up and sections follow distance along the road.
sections.watch_out: Layer heights must keep earthworks below paving, or the layering check fails.

sections.name: test_unrecognised_schedules_are_left_to_the_generic_packing
sections.title: Unknown schedule items are left unplaced
sections.what: Confirms that tasks with names the layout does not recognise produce no placed shapes and are reported as unplaced instead.
sections.why: Likely reason: so paperwork or general tasks do not appear as fake objects in the 3D view.

sections.name: test_building_storeys_stack_by_level_with_facade_and_roof
sections.title: Building floors stack with facade and roof
sections.what: Checks that floor slabs rise in fixed steps of four metres from a two-metre start, stay in the same spot, that curtain walls and foundations are recognised, that roof work sits above the top slab, and that equipment on a floor stays at that floor's position.
sections.why: Likely reason: to keep a building readable as stacked storeys with equipment inside it.
sections.watch_out: The height steps are fixed in this test, so changing floor spacing means updating it.

sections.name: test_airport_strips_lie_airside_of_the_terminal
sections.title: Airport strips sit airside of the terminal
sections.what: Checks that the runway, taxiway, apron and terminal sit in a set order across the site, that the runway is built on earthworks, and that a control tower is recognised.
sections.why: Likely reason: to keep the airside zones in the correct order relative to the terminal.
sections.watch_out: Reordering these zones would break the airside check.

sections.name: test_port_berths_face_the_sea_with_cranes_and_yard
sections.title: Port berths face the sea with cranes and yard
sections.what: Checks that container berths are placed side by side in numeric order, that ship-to-shore cranes are recognised, and that the container yard lies landward of the berths and the breakwater lies seaward.
sections.why: Likely reason: so the land side and sea side of a port appear in the right order.

sections.name: test_hydro_scheme_runs_from_intake_through_penstock_to_powerhouse
sections.title: Hydro scheme follows water from intake to powerhouse
sections.what: Checks that dam blocks are placed in order and recognised as dams, that the intake is upstream, that the steel pipe carrying water runs between the intake and the powerhouse, and that the spillway sits beyond the dam. It also checks that a mine tailings dam is classed as mining.
sections.why: Likely reason: so the hydro layout follows the path the water takes.
sections.watch_out: The pipe check also requires a non-zero rotation, so an unrotated pipe would fail.

sections.name: test_tunnel_bores_run_between_portals_with_the_tbm_at_the_face
sections.title: Tunnel bores run between portals with boring machine
sections.what: Checks that the northbound and southbound tunnel linings are placed in order, that the two bores sit at different positions, that the west and east portals (tunnel entrances) bracket the bores, and that the track slab, boring machine launch point, central station walls and pump station are each recognised correctly.
sections.why: Likely reason: so the metro shows its tunnels running between their entrances.
sections.watch_out: The pump station must not be treated as a station box, so changes to station recognition could misclassify it.

sections.name: test_treatment_works_follow_flow_order_and_batteries_form_rows
sections.title: Treatment works in flow order and battery rows
sections.what: Checks that wastewater stages (screens, aeration basin, clarifier, digester) are placed left to right in process order, and that battery containers form rows with each power converter level with its matching battery.
sections.why: Likely reason: process order and row alignment make the plant readable and pair equipment correctly.
sections.watch_out: The one-metre height tolerance for pairing a converter with its battery is a rule a layout change could break.

sections.name: test_power_lng_and_telecom_elements_use_their_own_models
sections.title: Power, LNG and telecom use their own models
sections.what: Checks that the gas turbine hall, heat recovery steam generator, transformer, LNG tank and telecom tower each map to their specific shape rather than a generic one.
sections.why: Likely reason: so each specialised item looks like what it is.
sections.watch_out: If a schedule name stops matching its specific shape, this test fails.

summary: Checks that the site layout for each industry type places parts where they should go, such as wind turbines in number order, solar blocks in a grid, and pipes along a rack, based on names in the schedule. Only the first four sections were provided, so the rest of the file is not described here.
purpose: Protects the rule that industry layouts follow their known arrangements, and that unrecognised schedules fall back to the generic layout.
why: Each industry uses its own arrangement, so a mistake would place equipment in the wrong order or position.
how: A helper collects the placed items whose path contains a given text. The wind turbine test builds ten turbines with three activities each plus a substation breaker, then checks numbering, foundation placement and substation position. The solar test builds nine blocks with piling and tracker activities plus inverters and a building, then checks the solar shapes, the grid, and that each inverter sits beside its block. The remaining tests are not included in the packet.
inputs: Lists of schedule path names built inside the tests.
outputs: Pass or fail results. Placed items are checked by position and shape.
risks: Position checks use exact comparisons with tolerance in some cases, so small changes in the layout rules can break them. The pattern of names used to recognise an industry must stay in step with the layout rules.
debug: Start with the failing test name. Print the layout for the paths in that test and compare positions with the expected order.
